dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that's a familiar face. Isn't that Wislawa?

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: #Why, if it isn't {NICKNAME}! Knew there'd be some big names here.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Let's get the official business over with first. Unfortunately, you're the first seller at the expo to receive a complaint. We've received word that the muskets you're selling are a few shots away from turning into scrap.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: Well, yeah. It's written here plain as day.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: "Muskets for sale. Condition: extremely poor. The internal grooves have been worn away, and the ammo might be damp. Best practice is to pray that it doesn't explode before each use."

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Wait, so you weren't speaking in code to cover your tracks?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yeah. Sometimes people bring stuff that needs to be kept on the down low, so they dress it up as junk beforehand. Happens on the black market all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: You're overthinking things here — this stuff really is junk. We were just gonna scrap them, but my superiors thought we might as well try and make some Mora off of 'em.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: And who knows? If the prayers are answered and the gun ends up firing a few times... The buyer hasn't totally wasted their money, have they?

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: I mean, a weapon on the brink of ruin that's still capable of considerable firepower... Doesn't that just scream "black market" to you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, but who would buy something like this?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Umm... maybe collectors who don't care if it works? And desperados who don't care if it explodes?
